source:
Game Name (working title)
LAST ROUTE
"No one knows why the road is still open."
Core Idea
You and up to 5 friends are driving one truck across a frozen mountain to deliver the last generator core to a dying town.
Without it...
Thousands of people freeze.
So turning back isn't an option.
Core Gameplay Loop
Drive ⬇ Reach checkpoint ⬇ Random event ⬇ Solve it together ⬇ Repair truck ⬇ Continue ⬇ Repeat ⬇ Final escape
The truck almost never stops for long. The journey is the game.
The BIG Hook
The Storm Changes Every Run.
Not just weather.
The storm changes the world.
Examples:
🌨 Heavy snow.
Visibility 5 metres.
🧊 Frozen lake.
Road disappears.
Drive over ice.
Risk breaking through.
🌲 Fallen trees.
Need axes.
⛰ Avalanche.
New road opens.
Old road closes.
📡 Strange radio signal.
Follow it...
Or ignore it.
🏚 Abandoned village appears.
Sometimes.
Not every run.
Every run feels different.
Player Jobs
Everyone naturally gets a role.
🚛 Driver
Can only focus on driving.
🗺 Navigator
Uses map.
Finds routes.
Reads signs.
🔧 Mechanic
Repairs truck.
Keeps engine alive.
Changes tyres.
📦 Scavenger
Searches buildings.
Gets fuel.
Food.
Medicine.
Parts.
🔦 Lookout
Uses binoculars.
Warns about danger.
Nobody is standing around.
The Horror
No zombie waves.
No screaming monster.
Something...
Is following the truck.
It never attacks directly.
Instead...
Fuel disappears.
Doors open.
Lights go out.
Tyre tracks appear beside yours.
Someone knocks...
But nobody is there.
The mystery is the horror.
Mid Game Twist
You discover...
Every abandoned truck looks exactly like yours.
Same number.
Same cargo.
Same scratches.
How?
Nobody knows.
Now players start theorising.
Final Act
The storm gets insane.
Truck barely works.
Visibility almost zero.
Radio cuts in.
Someone says...
"Don't let it overtake you."
Now everyone panics.
You don't even know what "it" is.
Ending
Reach the town.
Unload generator.
Lights come on.
Storm instantly stops.
Outside...
Your truck has six sets of footprints around it.
Nobody says anything.
Game ends.
Players immediately start discussing what happened.
Why I think this is stronger
The mystery is what people remember.
Not:
"Big monster killed me."
But:
"WHY WAS THERE ANOTHER TRUCK?"
Those kinds of mysteries create YouTube theory videos.
MVP (cheap version)
One truck.
One mountain road.
Three checkpoints.
10-15 random events.
One ending.
No giant open world.
No massive AI.
The game could be finished in about 20-30 minutes per run.
But here's the one thing I'd still change.
I wouldn't make it a pure horror game.
I'd make it 70% adventure, 30% horror.
If players are scared the whole time, the fear wears off. If most of the game is about teamwork, driving, and making decisions, then the strange moments hit much harder because they're unexpected.
One last thing: if your goal is a viral Roblox game, don't try to beat Dead Rails by adding more monsters or more mechanics. Beat it by making players ask one question after every run:
"Wait... what actually happened out there?"
That kind of mystery gives people a reason to replay, tell their friends, and watch theory videos. That's much harder to copy than just another survival game.

answers.ask: A mountain road with three checkpoints is a long strip - should it be one region-scale map, or three chapter maps joined at the checkpoints?
answers.answer: Use one compact region-scale mountain road with all three checkpoints along it. The MVP is one road and the journey should feel continuous, not split into separate chapter maps.

answers.ask: Should the abandoned village be a fixed location on the route, or does it need to be omittable since it only appears on some runs?
answers.answer: Make it omittable: it appears only on some runs as a random route-side event/location. It should not be a fixed required stop.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D cooperative adventure map set on one compact, continuous frozen mountain road crossing a stormy alpine region. A single truck route winds through snowbound slopes and tight mountain passes, with three checkpoints spaced along the journey toward a distant dying town in the background, the delivery destination. Route conditions can include deep snow with very short sightlines, a frozen lake crossing where the road vanishes beneath ice, fallen-tree blockages, and avalanche-altered sections where one path is closed and another is exposed. Place scattered abandoned trucks along the route, each visually identical to the players’ truck, plus occasional strange tyre tracks beside the road. An abandoned village sits off the roadside as an omittable, intermittent location rather than a fixed stop, with small buildings that can be searched. Near the final stretch, the road becomes almost obscured by the intensified storm before descending into the town.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Adventure, specifically a cooperative, story-led expedition; the mystery-horror tone is thematic rather than a second layout genre. The road, destination, and sequence of discoveries give the journey its directional pull.

### Shape and preset
Use `world-corridor`: one continuous mountain-road journey rather than separate chapters. It most closely matches the Guided Trail preset, retaining its directed route and distant destination, but the prompt overrides its pedestrian-trail emphasis with a truck-width alpine road and omits its required reveal-exit treatment.

### Config requirements
`path-trail` is visible geometry: the single ploughed, partially snow-buried truck road winding through passes from the opening to town. `landmark-focal` is visible geometry: the distant dying town remains a small, warm-lit destination on the horizon until the final descent. `hazard-kill` is visible geometry: unstable ice, blocked shoulders, deep snow, and avalanche-affected roadside danger shape the route. `terrain-relief` is visible geometry: steep alpine slopes, ridges, narrow passes, and avalanche scars define the corridor. `water-body` is visible geometry: a frozen lake crossing where the normal road disappears beneath ice. `building-interior` is visible geometry: the occasional abandoned village has small searchable buildings entered from the roadside. No invisible gameplay volumes are required.

### Layout components
Build one long but compact region-scale route, beginning at a snowbound mountain approach and ending in a descending final stretch into the distant town. Place three checkpoint waystations sequentially along the road, each a clear roadside pause landmark rather than a separate map. The middle route crosses a broad frozen lake; its road markings vanish into windblown ice. Other stretches thread tight rock-and-snow passes, include fallen-tree blockages, and show avalanche debris closing one roadside branch while exposing another passable branch. Scatter abandoned trucks beside the road, all visually identical to the player truck, and add intermittent parallel tyre tracks in the snow. Put the abandoned village off one roadside branch, with several small dark buildings; it is optional and must not interrupt the main route when absent. Intensify snow density and reduce visible road definition near the final descent. Natural cliffs, snowbanks, and storm fade form the boundary. Compose the route as a diagonal winding ribbon, with the town held in the far background beyond successive ridges.

### Render order
Use `topdown`: the continuous drivable route, lake crossing, and avalanche detours need a valid, readable connection before the isometric scene is dressed. This is not `authored_plan`, since it is neither a maze nor a racing circuit.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is large, driven by one compact region-scale road spanning three checkpoints and a final town approach. Theme: isolated alpine expedition, muted blue-white snowstorm, sparse warm lights, uncanny abandoned infrastructure. Use `tiered` for non-overhanging mountain relief, `P3` for entering village buildings from the exterior route, and `CHECK` for the frozen-lake water feature.
